objective: Stably sort constrained records by an explicit case-sensitive string order while preserving record identity and caller input.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Generic constraints and immutable sorting remain current TypeScript patterns.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Ordered named records are practical application data.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Deterministic collation, stable ties and copied containers transfer to other sort adapters.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Bounded names isolate the intermediate generic/sort objective.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Cloned records or environment-dependent ordering can silently break identity and consistent results.

defects: A-to-Z wording did not specify case, Unicode or collation.
Reference/senior used localeCompare while junior used relational comparison; those need not implement the same ordering in locale-aware hosts.
Cloning every record before sorting passed all old value-only checks.
rationale: Define case-sensitive UTF-16 code-unit ordering and align reference/senior to the existing junior relational comparator, preserving junior as a valid alternative. Specify stable ties, exact record references/opaque fields, unchanged frozen-capable dense input and independent mutable outer arrays, bounded through1000 records and200-unit names. Four runtime assertions cover mixed case, spaces, numeric text, accented/supplementary/private-use strings, repeated identical records, mutable outputs, empty/singleton input and1000 stable groups. Add a static Symbol-payload round trip. Target comparison-model nlogn with bounded name cost and linear output, explicitly without claiming a mandated built-in algorithm. An initial expected Unicode literal was incorrectly decoded in a test fixture; corrected before final selected execution and approval.

defects: Senior Object.assign contradicted the spread guidance and could invoke the legacy target prototype setter.
Shallow own string/Symbol metadata and no-op fresh-copy behavior were incomplete.

rationale: Retain spread reference/junior and change senior to spread with the same dependent generic signature. Add a boolean-field wrong-value static check while preserving the existing name rejection. Target linear copied-field work/output; metadata contents are not traversed. Product remains the declared return type rather than promising static visibility of arbitrary extra properties.

objective: Stably sort readonly Player rows by a typed text or numeric column without replacing records or mutating input.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Keyof columns and copied comparator sorts remain current TypeScript techniques.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Sorting tabular application rows is practical UI/data work.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Numeric versus textual order, stable ties and original identity transfer to other table helpers.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Three fixed Player keys and bounded data keep the foundational comparator lesson focused.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Cloned rows can break selection identity even when displayed sort values look correct.

defects: Character order lacked explicit case/Unicode semantics and input bounds.
A reference comment inaccurately described readonly as removing the runtime sort method rather than its mutating type interface.
Cloning all rows before sorting passed the old mapped-field assertions.
rationale: Keep all three correct raw comparators and qualify the readonly comment. Define bounded finite signed/fractional scores, case-sensitive UTF-16 text order without locale normalization, stable ties and exact row/metadata references in fresh mutable outputs. Three runtime assertions cover mixed text on both columns, signed-zero/fractional/extreme numeric ordering, frozen inputs, output independence, empty lists and1000 equal-key rows. Add readonly-input/mutable-output type evidence. Target nlogn in the bounded comparison-sort model and linear output without a built-in algorithm guarantee. The old senior remains a valid comparator alternative; no new learner algorithm restriction is inferred from the teaching scaffold.

objective: Read one typed saved setting or its default without writing to either source and without replacing falsy choices.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Partial, keyof and nullish fallback remain current TypeScript fundamentals.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Reading user preferences with defaults is practical settings work.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Missing versus falsy values and read-only lookups transfer to configuration helpers.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Three fixed typed keys keep this foundational lookup objective focused.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Caching a default into the caller object can break frozen configuration and change persisted choices.

defects: No-write behavior for saved values was implicit; the old DEFAULTS-only check missed writes to saved.
Nullish hints did not distinguish the valid Partial domain from invalid null values.
A lookup that writes its chosen value into saved passed all old cases.
rationale: Retain all correct boards, including the junior undefined branch; null is outside the valid typed domain, so that board is not falsely penalized. State inherited/missing/undefined behavior, preserved false/zero/signed-zero, bounded finite font sizes and unchanged saved/DEFAULTS with unrelated metadata ignored. Three runtime assertions inspect frozen explicit-undefined records, all defaults across calls, inherited signed-zero/false, empty null-prototype saved objects and100 opaque extra fields. Add a strict null-font rejection. Target constant one-key/default lookup independent of unrelated property count; no schema/profile mutation occurs.
